candidates.source_summary: A man who played a significant role in an organised crime group which supplied class A drugs across Rochdale has been jailed for 10 years and six months.
candidates.source_title: Organised crime gang ‘manager’ jailed for supplying class-A drugs - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A man who played a significant role in an organised crime group which supplied class A drugs across Rochdale has been jailed for 10 years and six months. An investigation into Haider Ali was launched following information received that a drug deal had taken place from a car parked in Baron Street, in Rochdale town centre, just before midnight on January 4, 2025. Officers began to follow the vehicle and when it came to a stop at a local petrol station, officers immediately executed a reinforced stop to prevent it from making off. Ali, who was travelling as a passenger, exited the vehicle and began to speedily walk away before officers detained him. Following searches, Ali was found to be in possession of more than £1,000 in cash, and two mobile phones, all of which were seized. Ali was arrested on suspicion of being concerned in the supply of class A drugs and taken to custody where further searches recovered two bundles of several wraps of a brown and a white substance. Tests later confirmed these substances to be heroin and cocaine. A pre-paid mobile phone seized from Ali was confirmed to be the Adam drug line. Following this, investigators also uncovered that Ali was not only dealing drugs at street level, but he was also managing other street dealers. Evidence suggested that Ali had progressed from being a street dealer in 2014 to holding a significant role within the Adam OCG in 2024 into 2025, managing street dealers and the dedicated dealer phone, and directing those below him on where there next deal is.

candidates.source_title: Warning to think twice about buying e-bikes and e-scooters this Christmas - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A hard-hitting warning has been issued about the dangers of illegal e-bikes and e-scooters as Christmas approaches. Greater Manchester Police and its partners are urging families to think carefully before buying off-road bikes, illegal e-bikes and e-scooters as Christmas gifts, warning that vehicles used unlawfully could be seized and destroyed — or lead to tragedy. The warning comes as part of Operation Hurricane, GMP’s coordinated crackdown on the anti-social and dangerous use of off-road bikes, e-bikes and quad bikes across Greater Manchester. One family which knows the devastating consequences they can cause is that of Jacob Calland, who died after being hit by a car while he was a passenger on an e-scooter when it went through a red light in Wythenshawe in March this year. He died from his injuries eight days later. Jacob’s mother, Carly Calland, said: “No words will ever be able to describe the pain caused by Jacob’s death. My heart has been smashed into a thousand pieces and there is nothing that can be done to fix it. My life is a living nightmare. “I climbed into the hospital bed to cuddle him and I fell asleep holding him. When I woke up, it was time to turn off the machines. I told Jacob I loved him just before he passed away. My baby boy was gone forever. “He won’t sit his GCSEs, he won’t have his sweet sixteen birthday party, he won’t go to his school prom. He won’t be able to follow his dreams. He won’t get married and won’t have children. His life ended the moment that collision happened.” The e-scooter rider, who was 14 at the time, received an 18-month youth referral order and a five-year driving ban after pleading guilty to causing death by dangerous driving, causing death by driving unlicensed, and causing death by driving uninsured.

candidates.source_summary: ROCHDALE'S Crown Oil Arena is a venue which will forever be etched into York City folklore.
candidates.source_title: Rochdale v York: Minstermen chase another milestone with 'caged lion' desperate to feature
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Some 204 days will have elapsed between the Minstermen's two visits there in 2026. Saturday's appointment will create nothing like the incredulous theatre of events on April 25, but the hope among the York contingent is that it produces another milestone moment, nevertheless. Back in late spring, York ended their decade-long absence from the Football League in the most scarcely-believable stoppage-time finale ever. On this occasion, the wait for the Minstermen revolves around securing their maiden away victory as an EFL club once again. Their last win on the road as a league club was back in September 2015. Scott Lindsey wasn't present in Lancashire, last time out, but he stressed that those astonishing scenes will form part of his pre-match preparations, as the majority of York players are still at the club. The York chief said: "I think it's important that the players feel that environment when they turn up at the stadium again. I can't comment on that because I obviously wasn't here then. "But all that they will remember are good memories from that stadium. And I think that is important. So we'll definitely be leaning on that. "I think it's important that we do mention it. "But it's for the players to remember those memories. It can only be a good thing that the last time they were there, what happened." The hero last time out was Josh Stones, whose 103rd-minute goal sparked ecstatic scenes among York's 1,500-following and 4,000-odd watching the beam-back at the LNER Community Stadium. Stones had done it tough since and is being integrated back into the first-team following a lumbar glute injury. Suffice to say, he is desperate to be involved at Dale. Lindsey added: "It's like caging a lion, isn't it? He'll be coming out of the traps ready to go again. "I think he showed some frustration in the fact that he didn't play in the Bradford game. He wanted to play, which is great. I want players who want to play, which is fantastic. "But we have to be really mindful of his load, bearing in mind he's been out for so long. And hopefully we get a fresher Josh Stones who can come on the pitch on Saturday and make a real impact. "And the more we do that, the closer we're getting to him to be a starter for us."

candidates.source_summary: Thousands of people across the borough gathered to honour the nation’s war heroes and pay their respects to those who have made sacrifices in defence of the country, with commemorations taking place on Remembrance Sunday and Armistice Day on Wednesday.
candidates.source_title: Residents praised for Remembrance tributes - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Thousands of people across the borough gathered to honour the nation’s war heroes and pay their respects to those who have made sacrifices in defence of the country, with commemorations taking place on Remembrance Sunday and Armistice Day on Wednesday. Representatives from the Navy, Army and Royal Air Force joined veterans and civic dignitaries for parades and services in Rochdale town centre, Castleton, Heywood, Littleborough, Middleton, Norden, Milnrow and Wardle. Residents gathered as memorials fell silent, with the Last Post played at each service. Each included the immemorial words from Laurence Binyon’s 1914 poem, For the Fallen: “They shall grow not old as we that are left grow old; Age shall not weary them, nor the years condemn; at the going down of the sun and in the morning. We will remember them.” Praising the tributes, Mayor of Rochdale Cllr Faisal Rana, said: “The turnout across the borough was incredible, as people of all ages gathered at memorials in Heywood, Middleton, Pennines, and Rochdale to pay their respects. “On a poignant and moving Remembrance Day, we honoured the fallen, people of all faiths and no faith, from countries all over the world. It was a day when the whole community fell silent to reflect and remember. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale have signed midfielder Jamie Allen on a short-term contract. Allen, 31, returns to the club where he began his career and made more than 150 appearances before his exit in 2017. He went to Burton Albion before a move to Coventry City two years later where he spent the next seven seasons. Allen won two promotions with the Sky Blues, played in the Championship play-off final in 2023 and made the last of his 200 appearances for the club in their final league game of last season before being released in the summer - and he now becomes part of Ian Watson's Dale squad. "I always thought I'd come back some day," he told the club's website . "The club has been a huge part of my life. It's been a weird summer for me. I reached out to Rochdale in pre-season to train and keep fit, which I've enjoyed. "I've got a good relationship with the gaffer. I appreciate what he's done for me and thankful that I've got a deal at the end of it." candidates.source_title: Ollie Banks ready to end away day dip as York City head to old foes Rochdale - The York Press
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Ollie Banks assured there were no concerns in the dressing room with York City’s away form – but wants nothing more than to end their winless run on the road this Saturday. Banks was a part of the York squad that embarked on an incredible 18 match unbeaten run away from home in the National League last season, as City went on to clinch the title. But since promotion to League Two, it’s been much more of a challenge for the Minstermen to find wins away from the LNER Community Stadium. With three draws and four defeats from City’s seven matches on the road, only 17th-placed Bristol Rovers and 19th-placed Port Vale have worse records away from home. City have the chance to rectify that record when travelling to old foes Rochdale this Saturday, with Banks keen to play his part in rewarding the visiting supporters. “In the group, in our meetings and in training when we’re going into an away game, there’s nothing really surrounding it that worries us,” Banks told The Press. “I think in a lot of the games away from home, we’ve probably deserved a win. “There’s been a couple where we haven’t been at it, but we definitely should have had at least two or three wins away from home.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: York City travel to Rochdale tomorrow (Saturday) for their Sky Bet League Two fixture, with kick-off at 3pm. The Minstermen are looking to record their first away victory of the 2026/27 season. The game takes York back to a ground that holds special memories. Last season they went to Rochdale needing a single point to clinch top spot and promotion, in a winner-takes-all clash in which Rochdale were also title contenders. Mani Dieseruvwe put the home side ahead late on, but York had one final chance and Josh Stones forced the ball over the line in the 103rd minute to send York back into the Football League. Rochdale went on to win the play-offs and joined York in the EFL. Rochdale have struggled to get going since returning to League Two, losing four of their first five games. They sit 20th in the table with four wins to their name. They needed extra time to beat Accrington Stanley in the Emirates FA Cup, and their latest league game was a 4-2 defeat at Port Vale two weeks ago. York went out of the Jersey Mike’s Trophy after a defeat at Bradford City. Before that, they beat Northampton Town 4-0 in the FA Cup. In all-time head-to-head meetings, York just edge Rochdale, with 51 wins to Rochdale’s 46.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: An office building which has been empty for almost a decade is being turned into flats. Alam Investments has been granted planning permission by Rochdale Council to turn the former office building at St James Place, 168 Yorkshire Street, in Rochdale town centre, into 21 self-contained apartments. The redevelopment of the three-storey building will include a mix of 17 one-bedroom flats and four two-bedroom flats. Planning documents submitted with the application state: “The building has been vacant for approximately eight years and is in need of investment and reuse. “The proposed scheme will bring the property back into productive use, provide much-needed housing in a sustainable location, and contribute positively to the vitality and regeneration of Rochdale town centre. “The property lies adjacent to notable heritage assets, including St Mary’s Ukrainian Catholic Church (Grade II listed), and is surrounded by a mix of commercial and residential uses. “In terms of heritage value, the building itself is of limited architectural and historic significance, lacking distinctive features of merit. Its primary contribution to the conservation area arises from its form, scale, and materiality, which ensure a degree of consistency within the surrounding townscape. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Springhill Hospice has reported a series of thefts and attempted break-ins at its charity shops this week, with replacement windows at its Emporium expected to cost around £2,000. The hospice said it is working with Greater Manchester Police following incidents at the Emporium and its Oldham Road shop. Thieves initially damaged a window at Springhill Emporium but failed to gain entry, according to the hospice. The premises were targeted again on Tuesday 10 November, when a window was damaged and items were stolen. The hospice estimates that replacing the large windows will cost around £2,000. Its Oldham Road shop was targeted on Thursday night, 12 November, with further damage and losses reported. Springhill said the incidents had devastated staff, who work alongside the local community to raise money to keep hospice services running for Rochdale residents. The hospice is working with Greater Manchester Police and hopes to release further information to help identify those responsible. Anyone with information about the incidents is asked to contact Greater Manchester Police.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Microsoft 365 disruption has prompted Rochdale-based award-winning IT provider, No Fuss IT, to encourage businesses to look beyond everyday technical support and consider how they would keep communicating if their usual email service became unavailable. No Fuss IT, whose IT team is led by Finn O’Loughlin, provides email continuity as part of its enhanced approach to proactively supporting businesses, including organisations working towards or maintaining ISO 9001 and ISO 27001 requirements. When email stops working, the consequences can reach much further than an empty inbox. Customer enquiries can go unanswered. Purchase orders can be delayed. Staff can lose access to conversations they need to complete their work, while managers spend time finding out what is happening and deciding what to do next. For businesses affected by the latest Microsoft disruption over the last 24 hours, it raises a practical question. If the main route into your email becomes unavailable, have you got another way through? Think of it like a motorway with an alternative toll road. Most days, the motorway gets everyone where they need to go. It is familiar, convenient and part of the daily routine. But when a major incident closes the carriageway, everyone relying on that same route can find themselves stuck. Knowing that someone is working to reopen it does little to move the queue.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale Borough Council’s staff-run charity is collecting new, unwrapped gifts across more than 40 drop-off points ahead of Friday, December 11 Rochdale Borough Council’s staff-run charity, Number One Riverside Giving Back, is now collecting donations for this year’s Christmas Toy Appeal. The annual campaign helps ensure children living in poverty across the borough have presents to open on Friday, December 25. Organised by council staff for the past 13 years, the appeal is accepting donations at borough libraries and Your Trust leisure centres until Friday, December 11. Last year, volunteers distributed a record 10,000 toys to around 3,000 children, building on a programme that has brought festive cheer to thousands of youngsters since 2013. Council policy advisor Helen Walton, from the Giving Back charity, said: “Christmas should be a magical time for every child, but for many families the financial pressures they face mean that even a small gift can feel impossible to afford. We’re already seeing requests for help, and that’s why every donation matters. "Knowing there’s something to unwrap on Christmas morning will mean the world to a child. We’re incredibly grateful for the continued kindness of our communities, whose support helps bring joy and hope to families when they need it most.” To take part, supporters simply need to donate a new, unwrapped gift suitable for a child or teenager up to age 16. Alongside libraries and leisure centres, collection points are open at the first-floor management office at Rochdale Riverside, The Trade Centre UK at Sandbrook Park, and The Old Police Station in Heywood. A full list of more than 40 drop-off locations and alternative ways to support the campaign is available at rochdale.gov.uk/ChristmasToyAppeal . Organisers are also encouraging residents to shop sustainably within the borough where possible, though every donation is warmly welcomed regardless of size. Supporters who prefer to shop online can have gifts delivered directly to Giving Back - Christmas Toy Appeal, Rochdale Borough Council, Number One Riverside, Smith Street, Rochdale OL16 1XU. All postal deliveries must arrive by Friday, December 11, so volunteers have time to sort and distribute them before Christmas Day.

The work, to the east of the city centre on the historic Rochdale Canal, is part of the Canal and River Trust's extensive programme of winter repairs covering 2,000 miles of waterway. The waterway opened in 1804 as the first of three trans-Pennine canals, running between Manchester and Sowerby Bridge, West Yorkshire. The charity, which cares for canals and waterways across England and Wales, said it would be carrying out hundreds of projects over the next five months to maintain the 'living heritage' of the network that was built in the industrial revolution and still functions today. The new lock gates in Manchester have been handcrafted from oak at the Canal and River Trust's lock gate workshop at Stanley Ferry, Yorkshire, before being craned into place. Each leaf of the upstream gate weighs 1.5 tonnes, with the downstream leaves weighing 2.5 tonnes, and replace gates that were installed around the turn of the millennium, the charity said. candidates.source_title: Lest We Forget: borough falls silent to mark Remembrance Day – Rochdale Borough Council
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Thousands gathered across the borough for Remembrance Day services to honour the nation’s war heroes and pay their respects to those who have made sacrifices in defence of the country. Representatives from the Navy, Army and Royal Air Force joined veterans and civic dignitaries for parades and services in Rochdale town centre, Castleton, Heywood, Littleborough, Middleton, Norden, Milnrow and Wardle. Residents gathered as memorials fell silent, with the Last Post played at each service. Each included the immemorial words from Laurence Binyon’s 1914 poem, For the Fallen: “They shall grow not old as we that are left grow old; Age shall not weary them, nor the years condemn; at the going down of the sun and in the morning. We will remember them.” The Armed Forces community, Members of Parliament, Mayor of Rochdale, Council Leader, Councillor Neil Emmott, councillors, faith leaders, local schools and members of the public also laid their own wreaths and gave respects, following moving readings of The Kohima Epitaph: “When you go home, tell them of us and say, for your tomorrow, we gave our today.” Mayor of Rochdale, Councillor Faisal Rana, said: “The turnout across the borough was incredible, as people of all ages gathered at memorials in Heywood, Middleton, Pennines, and Rochdale to pay their respects. On a poignant and moving Remembrance Day, we honoured the fallen, people of all faiths and no faith, from countries all over the world. It was a day when the whole community fell silent to reflect and remember. “We will forever hold a special place in our hearts, today and always, for those who never came home. Without their selfless dedication and sacrifices, the freedom, liberty and values we take for granted would have been lost. Side by side they fought together, they fell together and secured the peace together. We will always remember them. Lest we forget.” Current or former Armed Forces personnel can register for help or get more information by visiting the Armed forces community page.

candidates.source_title: Prime Minister Andy Burnham backs new city centre 'express' bus service
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has backed calls for the return of an ‘express’ bus service from Heywood to Manchester. The 167 bus service was scrapped 14 years ago, but there have been growing calls for its return. Heywood and Middleton MP Elsie Blundell has pushed for the route to be reinstated since she was elected in 2024. It is understood that the re-imagined 167 bus route would start in Norden, then stop at Bamford, Heywood and Rhodes before heading into the city centre. Mrs Blundell believes the return of the express bus service would be boost the local economy as well as improving transport connectivity between Heywood and the city centre. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter Speaking in the House of Commons this week, Mrs Blundell said: “Heywood is the largest town in Greater Manchester without an express bus service into Manchester city centre . “This is something I have pushed for since my election because I know this will transform the lives of the people in my constituency and it will transform the economy there. “What can the government do to support Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) to deliver this service and make sure people in Heywood will have the benefit of buses placed back under public control?” Mrs Blundell believes the express bus can act as a ‘stopgap’ for Heywood residents while they wait for Metrolink trams to be brought into the area. Metrolink coming to Heywood has not been confirmed, but TfGM said previously they are working on a business case for the project. In his response, Prime Minister Andy Burnham criticised the Conservatives opposite him in the chamber for privatising the bus system in the 1980s. Don't let an algorithm decide what Manchester news you see - click here to add the MEN as your preferred Google source Mr Burnham said: “We all remember when the party opposite me deregulated buses in this country and left people paying high bus fares – and they still are in many parts of the country because they are still deregulated. They pay £3 or £4 for a single journey and many other constituencies. “We will put a £2 cap on these bus fares next year. Because we put buses back under public control in Greater Manchester, and because we reversed 40 years of deregulation, we can introduce the service my honourable friend is calling for. “I used to support it in my previous job. I can’t speak for the current mayor of Greater Manchester, but I hope she does the same.” Bev Craig, Mr Burnham’s successor as mayor of Greater Manchester, has not publicly declared her support for the return of the 167. However, it is understood she has met with the Heywood and Middleton North MP to discuss her case for the express bus service and Heywood Metrolink. TfGM confirmed they have modelled various options to assess cost, estimated passenger demand/revenue and economic benefits of bringing the 167 into the transport network. More work is needed before any further development takes place, it is understood. The mayor’s election manifesto did commit to growing the Bee Network. Since being elected, night buses have been introduced to every part of Greater Manchester as well as other improvements.

candidates.source_summary: A partnership which links cutting-edge research with innovative businesses has won a top award for recycling carbon fibre waste.
candidates.source_title: Partnership wins award for manufacturing innovation - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A partnership which links cutting-edge research with innovative businesses has won a top award for recycling carbon fibre waste. The Centre of Expertise in Advanced Materials and Sustainability (CEAMS) and its project partners have been recognised nationally after winning the Sustainability and Circularity Award at the Composites UK Industry Awards. The award recognises pioneering work that could help transform how carbon fibre waste is reused across the aerospace sector and wider manufacturing industries. Working alongside Cygnet Texkimp, SHD Composites, NCC and Teledyne CML Composites, CEAMS successfully demonstrated a world-first aerospace component manufactured using material containing 100% recycled continuous carbon fibre. The project showed that recycled carbon fibre can achieve levels of stiffness and strength comparable to new material, while using existing industrial manufacturing processes. This creates a realistic route for large-scale adoption across advanced manufacturing sectors. Previous CEAMS research estimated that recycled continuous carbon fibre may reduce carbon emissions by up to 80% when compared with new material, while helping create more resilient UK supply chains and higher-value uses for composite waste.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Residents are being asked to help make a difference to families in need this Christmas. Rochdale Council’s staff-run charity Number One Riverside Giving Back has started collecting donations for this year’s Christmas Toy Appeal. The annual appeal, organised by council staff for the past 13 years, is accepting donations at local libraries or Your Trust leisure centres until Friday, December 11. Council policy advisor Helen Walton, of the Giving Back charity, said: “Christmas should be a magical time for every child, but for many families the financial pressures they face mean that even a small gift can feel impossible to afford. “We’re already seeing requests for help, and that’s why every donation matters. Knowing there’s something to unwrap on Christmas morning will mean the world to a child. Helen Walton meets some of the team from Renold Gears in Littleborough who donated gifts from customers and staff to boost last year’s appeal “We’re incredibly grateful for the continued kindness of our communities, whose support helps bring joy and hope to families when they need it most.”

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A unique cafe has opened it's doors in the heart of Rochdale's countryside this summer, with the caveat that it is unreachable by car. The Caravan Cafe, a hidden walker's stop in the heart of Norden village's countryside operated by Heather Brierley, offers a reprieve for hikers, walkers, and cyclists a ' bru-with-a-view'. Opening it's doors in May 2026 after positive community feedback from local walkers in the area, The Caravan Cafe has been slowly gaining traction through word-of-mouth and on it's Facebook page. Heather said: "It's the best thing I ever did. I wish I'd done it years ago when my Dad was alive. I hope he's proud, and he can see I'm not just a townie." "The support I've gotten from people is unbelievable." Caravan Cafe's welcoming appeal has been reflected in it's decor, outfitted with a variety of Heather's handmade assets, pieces from her parents, and community donations of furniture. Although customers are not able to enter the titular caravan , the outside seating area boasts scenic views of the Rochdale countryside. Heather shared: "I'm happier in myself. It helps my mental health, and it's a humbling passion. […] I'm lucky to share this."

candidates.source_summary: Fire festival returns to Rochdale with free entry and Christmas lights switch-on About Manchester
candidates.source_title: Fire festival returns to Rochdale with free entry and Christmas lights switch-on - About Manchester
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Final preparations are under way for Ignite Fire Festival taking place at Rochdale Town Hall Square from Friday 20 to Sunday 22 November, leading up to the much anticipated Christmas lights switch-on at the town hall. Ignite Fire Festival, sponsored by car supermarket The Trade Centre UK, will be transforming the square and gardens around Rochdale Town Hall, including the new pathways and parkland on Broadfield Slopes. This free night-time event will open 5pm – 8pm, delivering a magical trail of fire, lights and sound. Organisers Rochdale Development Agency say this year will be the best yet with new dazzling trails and attractions. Immersive night-time trail, ‘BODY,’ will take centre stage, bringing visitors on a journey through six zones of the human body using fire, light, sound and special effects. The multi-sensory experience is the most ambitious fire and light installation yet from multi-award-winning outdoor arts specialists Walk the Plank, and Ignite will be its north-west premiere, after having previously travelled over the globe, from Ireland to Canada. Audiences can expect to be mesmerised on a dramatic, spellbinding journey as they walk through the glowing embers of human metabolism – the silent furnace that keeps us alive, continuously generating heat to power all the body’s functions. Using cutting-edge technology, the experience will entertain and educate, providing a deeper understanding of what lies beneath. There will also be a Fire Garden providing extra sparkle, illuminating slopes and gardens behind Rochdale Town Hall with pyrotechnics, transforming it into a place of beauty. Back again for 2026 is ‘Drum Machine’ – the 20-strong drumming collective who will be bringing their dance floor grooves and stomping tunes to the festival. Also returning are ‘Fireflies,’ as part of the Culture Co-op programme with Rochdale’s Skylight Circus Arts, and live fire shows by interactive arts group Travelling Light Circus, alongside residents trained up especially for Ignite, performing fire spinning feats. There will be flame-cooked hot food served each night including Texas BBQ, brisket, mac n cheese, Bratwurst and seasonal drinks. And look out for stalls filled with homemade goods from fantastic local young people – a Teenage Market will also be staged each evening at the event. On the opening night (Friday November 20) from 5.30pm to 7.30pm, you can take part in an Ignite themed ‘Paint the Flame’ pottery painting at Clay & Glaze on Drake Street, a short walk from the festival. You can paint a fire or a dragon-themed mug. The activity is suitable for children and adults. (Charge of £10 per mug applies). Father Christmas and his special guests, including the Mayor of Rochdale, Councillor Faisal Rana , stars from Middleton Arena’s pantomime Cinderella, the borough’s children’s champions and local members of the UK Youth Parliament switch-on the Christmas lights at 5.30pm on Sunday (22 November). The switch-on takes place in front of the town hall after the traditional countdown, whilst Ignite Fire Festival continues until 8pm.

candidates.source_summary: Tributes paid to former Rochdale Councillor About Manchester
candidates.source_title: Tributes paid to former Rochdale Councillor - About Manchester
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Tributes have been paid to former Rochdale councillor, Shaun O’Neill. Shaun was a councillor representing the Healey Ward for many years, serving on many committees, and was also a longstanding representative of the Fire Brigades Union. Tributes have today been paid to Shaun by the Leader of the Council and the Mayor of Rochdale. Councillor Neil Emmott, leader of the council, said: “Shaun’s sudden and tragic death has rocked everyone who knew him. He was a man of great integrity, principle and compassion who got on with the job in hand in his own quiet and unassuming way. Shaun was in politics for the right reasons, to improve people’s lives, tackle inequalities and fight for a better world. That was what moved him. On a personal level, I always found Shaun to be a loyal and supportive colleague who cared deeply for the people he represented. He will be deeply missed. My thoughts are with his family and many friends at this time.” Councillor Faisal Rana, Mayor of Rochdale, said: “The death of Shaun is absolutely devastating news, which will leave a considerable void across the community and in the lives of all who knew him. Shaun was a fine colleague, always supportive with a kind word and wise counsel. He was widely trusted, principled and admired across the political divide. A light has gone out across the community at Shaun’s untimely passing. Condolences to his family at this sad time.” If you would like to contribute to About Manchester, contact us here .

candidates.source_title: Council issues admissions reminder to parents before the New Year – Rochdale Borough Council
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Parents who have children starting primary school next September are being reminded to apply for their child’s school place before Friday 15 January 2027. While the New Year deadline feels quite a distance away to some, data held by Rochdale Borough Council shows families still miss this important deadline. In 2026, 216 parents submitted a late primary school application. This led to more than a third of those children (37%) missing out on their first preferred school as a result when reception started this September. In comparison, 89% of those who submitted an application on time secured their preferred school. Councillor Rachel Massey, cabinet member for children’s services and education, said: “We know life is busy for families, especially when your children are a lot younger, but it is so important to get your school applications in on time. “While the deadline is in the New Year, January will be here before we know it, so I urge all families to get their applications in as soon as they can to give your child the best possible chance of securing their preferred primary school.”

candidates.source_summary: A 39-year-old man has been arrested after police found what they believe to be an air pistol near a remembrance ceremony in Rochdale town centre.
candidates.source_title: Man arrested for possessing an imitation firearm at Rochdale Armistice Day event
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A 39-year-old man has been arrested after police found what they believe to be an air pistol near a remembrance ceremony in Rochdale town centre. Greater Manchester Police said officers approached the man at about 11.30am, this morning, Wednesday 11 November, after he appeared to be protesting near the ceremony. Officers said they had reasonable grounds to search him and found what is believed to be an air pistol. He was arrested on suspicion of possession of an imitation firearm and remains in custody while enquiries continue. No injuries have been reported and police said there is currently no evidence to suggest the air pistol was fired. Police confirmed the man did not interrupt the service and was standing some distance from the main ceremony. There’s less than a fortnight to go until local educators are recognised for their outstanding contributions to the lives of children and young people. The awards, which take place on Friday, November 20, at Rochdale Town Hall, celebrate the achievements of local teachers, tutors, support staff and other education professionals who help to give children and young people the best start in life. Now in its third year, the event continues to grow from strength to strength with a record number of 896 nominations submitted this year. Eighteen awards will be presented on the night, including Raising Rochdale School or College of the Year and Leadership Team of the Year. Other highly competitive categories include Primary Teacher of the Year, Secondary Teacher of the Year and Post-16 Tutor of the Year.
